HRA Analysis: An intriguing small stand-start field kicks off tonight, where TULLAH GIRL (4) looks well placed off the 10 metres. She was narrowly beaten here two starts ago before being somewhat disappointing last week, but in the small field you would expect her to get her chance to run over the top of them. ONEHANDONEBOUNCE (5) brings similar form lines and is another who should appreciate the small field after a handy third when doing all the work three wide two starts back. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (6) is clearly the class horse of the field, and if he begins as swiftly as he can, he may be able to make up the ground very quickly and be driven confidently here. FLEETWOOD ROCK (2) was well backed but galloped out at the same venue two starts ago, although a better beginning could leave him as a rough hope here. DENNY (1) isn't going as badly as his form suggests and should get his chance from the pole draw off the front mark. Selections: TULLAH GIRL (4), ONEHANDONEBOUNCE (5), ROCKANDHARDPLACE (6), FLEETWOOD ROCK (2)

OUTBACK LASS (1) drew the pole and was an easy winner against a similar field last start, so will look to replicate that performance again here. FEELINKINDALUCKY (6) should get his chance following her everywhere she goes and should appreciate getting back to the pegs close to the speed. TUFFTIGER (4) was good first up for the new stable but draws an awkward gate here. Expect they may roll forward and try dictate the speed outside the expected leader and favourite. PARK LANE (7) will have to be driven more conservatively this week from the back row but could run into a placing if the race becomes pegs dominated, which may make it difficult for the rest of the field to get into the finish. Selections: OUTBACK LASS (1), FEELINKINDALUCKY (6), TUFFTIGER (4), PARK LANE (7)

GEMMY LOU (1) battled on gamely last start at the same track and distance but draws the ideal pole position here, which should make her extremely hard to beat. More than confident she can lead all the way. KING BART (3) drops back somewhat in grade and should find a spot on speed, which should see him right in the finish. OUR SWEET TRIXIE (8) has been racing consistently in stronger races than what she meets here and, although she will likely have to come with one run, can't be ruled out. IDEN REGAL WAVE (6) and STANTON BREAK (7) will look to duck to the pegs and hope the gaps appear late, which would give them both first-four chances. Selections: GEMMY LOU (1), KING BART (3), OUR SWEET TRIXIE (8), IDEN REGAL WAVE (6)

Another race where the pole marker BABY CHARLOTTE (1) looks extremely hard to beat. Her recent effort when doing all the work outside the leader in handy time and sticking on well for second should make her very hard to beat here. Expect she should have enough gate speed to hunt through early and hold the front, and even over the middle distance, she clearly looks the one to beat. HIGH FROSTY (5) was well backed and a dominant winner first up at this track, aided by some solid mid-race tempo. From the draw, he will need something similar here, but expect him to be running home strongly yet again. OSCAR MAC (6) should follow the expected favourite everywhere she goes and gets his chance to run into a placing, while VITESSE (3) is a four-year-old mare on debut whose two trials thus far have been handy enough. Expect her to put some wins together soon for her patient connections. Selections: BABY CHARLOTTE (1), HIGH FROSTY (5), OSCAR MAC (6), VITESSE (3)

Another stand-start event where manners will be key, but it is hard to go past LIKEABLE ROGUE (2) after his last-start victory, when an easy winner in the heat of this race. In the bigger field, he will need to be on his best behaviour and step away safely this time, but from the draw he looks one of the better chances. MIKI SANZ (3) is always thereabouts in these sorts of races and expect him to sit on speed and run his usual honest race. SETTEBELLO (1) was somewhat disappointing in the heat when having every chance in front, but may get his chance to redeem himself with a quick beginning and give them something to chase at odds. The runners off the 10-metre handicap will need some pressure throughout to allow them to get into the finish, but can't be ruled out for exotics, led by MAJOR DAVVIN (8), who should benefit being second up from a decent break. Selections: LIKEABLE ROGUE (2), MIKI SANZ (3), SETTEBELLO (1), MAJOR DAVVIN (8),

Expect some good tempo early here, with numerous horses possessing sharp gate speed engaged off the front row, which should again play into the hands of KENYA (8), who is threatening to break through after some good seconds of late. He was narrowly defeated in track-record time when coming with one run at them two starts ago at this track, and similar tactics should see him right in the firing line again. KNOCK OUT (7) gets the nice trailing draw and drops back in grade. If he puts his best foot forward, expect him to be running home strongly. SUMTHIN ELSE (1) gets the pole draw around the tight circuit and has her chance to improve, although she may cop some pressure from runners drawn wider. EYE SEE AMOUR (4) and QUEENOFDANCE (5) have been in good form of late but will need good drives and some luck in transit to be in the finish from their wide front-row draws. Selections: KENYA (8), KNOCK OUT (7), SUMTHIN ELSE (1), QUEENOFDANCE (5)

The standing-start event over the short trip, where CINCINNATI (1) will look to step cleanly from the tapes, as he did last start when second in a similar grade. He looked to have every chance that day when defeated by COLORADO GIRL (5), who won with somewhat ease and again draws the 10-metre mark here. A repeat performance from her would make her hard to hold out late. SMOOTH DEAL (2) is known for pinging the tapes and could run a race at odds if he finds the pegs first, although he will need to improve on his performance from last Sunday. RANIERI (3) and NO NUKES SKIPPER (8) look the best of the rest on current form. Selections: COLORADO GIRL (5), CINCINNATI (1), RANIERI (3), NO NUKES SKIPPER (8)

The highest-class event of the night from behind the mobile, where SOHO TIGER LILY (1) and WEONA EAGLE (2), both possessing very sharp gate speed, draw well. You would expect SOHO TIGERLILY (1) to hold the front and she could take some running down. However, she has done her best racing over the mile trip, so if she cops pressure at any stage, she could become somewhat vulnerable late. FAMILY REASONS (3) and HAY MIKI (4) have been competing in stronger races than what they meet here and will be hoping to slot into the running line, where both should be in the finish if they hold their form. INTO THE HARKNESS (7) could be the one at odds if she puts her best foot forward, having run a good second behind a handy one two starts back. From the nice trailing back-row draw, she could be finishing strongly with some tempo throughout. Selections: FAMILY REASONS (3), SOHO TIGER LILY (1), INTO THE HARKNESS (7), WEONA EAGLE (2) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:TECHYS WISH (6) started her career in winning fashion on October 17 at West Wyalong. She ran a fast last quarter in 27.6 after leading. This is a step up to racing the older mares, but she looks to have some class. ROCK POSTER (9) is the best-rated horse in this field and gets into the field with a claim drive from Riley Pace. She has had three starts back this preparation and won nicely last start at Kilmore. That was Riley’s first drive on the mare, and they looked to click well. She found gaps late, flashing home from last to win comfortably. MISS PIGGY WIGGY (5) is a mare with a nice turn of foot who is racing well. She worked forward, led and won comfortably three starts ago at Shepparton. Last start, she was narrowly beaten after sustaining a strong three-wide trip. She is racing well. OVER THE LINE (8) comes into this race nicely if she gets some luck. She has been checked in her last two starts, so you can put a line through those runs. Before that, she won well at Charlton when flashing home from last. She performs well for Ewa Justice, who takes the reins here. Also respecting the NSW visitor KEAYANG LADYBUG (2) from the barrier. SELECTIONS: TECHYS WISH (6), ROCK POSTER (9), MISS PIGGY WIGGY (5), OVER THE LINE (8)

OVERVIEW: This looks to be a very even field, which will benefit horses who can find some luck here. ALDEBARAN MISTIQUE (6) is a nice mare who does rely on a bit of luck, but she’s consistent and rarely runs a bad race. Donna Castles’ team is performing nicely. If she can slot into a good position, she is right in this. KALARNEY PRINCE (4) is the flashy grey who is hard to miss. He’s been racing at his best recently. He had to do it tough last start but still battled on well for fourth. ALDEBARAN MARCUS (7) is stuck on the fence here, but he is a nice horse in this grade. If he can get close enough, he will be right there in the finish. WOMAN TO LOVE (5) was probably hoping for a better barrier here, but much like many of the other runners in this field, if she can find some luck with the race map, she is a winning chance. Also respecting PATNWILL (3), who could be a good-value performer here if he can find the fence with his nice gate speed. JAKEE BOY (9) is also a smart trotter, but he can do things wrong. SELECTIONS: ALDEBARAN MISTIQUE (6), KALARNEY PRINCE (4), ALDEBARAN MARCUS (7), WOMAN TO LOVE (5)

OVERVIEW: It’s hard to narrow it down to just four runners here. Trainer Jeff Tabone has two interesting runners in this event, EVERY CENT COUNTS (1) and FEAR THE MISSUS (2). They both have very similar form, with two starts each in the heats and final of the $100,000 Australian Pacing Gold series in June. FEAR THE MISSUS (2) finished last in his final in a race won by the exciting CARDIGAN SNIPER, while EVERY CENT COUNTS (1) finished a well-beaten fourth in her final, which was won by super filly IDEAL FRANKIE. Both their final runs were not bad performances in such tough fields, particularly given their limited experience heading into the races. They have both won Bacchus Marsh trials and find a much easier race here first-up. I’m probably sticking with FEAR THE MISSUS (2) on top, but it is hard to split the two. SONOFPLATINUM (4) looks to be getting better with each start, and I’ve quite liked his last two runs. Two starts ago, he flashed home along the sprint lane from well back to finish a close second. Last start, he was held up late, but once he got out, he let down nicely. With some luck here, we could see the best version of this horse. JUST MY LUCK (7) did all the work last start and was beaten by some swoopers late, but he’s racing OK. LUNA ROSSA (9) and ALCATRAZ MISS (8) are also winning chances. BACK: FEAR THE MISSUS (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: FEAR THE MISSUS (2), EVERY CENT COUNTS (1), SONOFPLATINUM (4), JUST MY LUCK (7)

OVERVIEW:TRYX VIXEN (2) is a smart filly who got back into the winner’s circle last start. Her run was huge. She drew barrier 11 and was wide for most of the race, covering an extra 45 metres. Barrier two is much better, and a gear change has been noted, with the headcheck removed and a different bit applied. MAJOR ORION (1) looks to be her biggest danger here from the barrier. She raced in the breeze last start outside feature race-winning smart filly Delizioso and still battled on strongly for third. The fence is the place to be on this track, and that’s where she will be. WHERES WOOD WOOD (4) is racing well, having won two of her last three starts. Last start, she finished fifth, but she was held up going into the straight and still let down OK. Trainer Wayne Lear is chasing his 100th training victory here. TOORAM DANNY (6) is a smart horse who is lightly raced and in good form. He rarely runs a bad race, but his barrier is difficult here. BACK: TRYX VIXEN (2)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: TRYX VIXEN (2), MAJOR ORION (1), WHERES WOOD WOOD (4), TOORAM DANNY (6)

OVERVIEW:LENNY LINCOLN (7) is first-up here for NSW trainer Darrell Hillier after racing for most of his career in Queensland. He is a 10-time winner and won a recent trial for his new team at Leeton. He will likely appreciate the change in scenery, but he’s a bit of a risk here first-up. COLBY ART (6) is another horse who is first-up for a new trainer here. He’s spent the last few years in Tasmania and is now in Victoria in the care of local trainer Wayne Lear. He could appreciate the change in scenery too, but it is a tricky barrier first-up. YANKEE BABE (1), despite not having the best numerical form, has the best sectional times in this field. The fence trip suits on this track, but my only concern is that she can lack gate speed, and GOODTIME MAE (2), TREACHEROUSTIMES (4) and COLBY ART (6) can all fly the arm. METRO MEMORY (8) is a good sit sprinter who rarely runs a bad race and gets a good barrier to follow through early. Also respecting ENABLE ME (3), who was second when returning last start and should improve here. SELECTIONS: LENNY LINCOLN (7), COLBY ART (6), YANKEE BABE (1), METRO MEMORY (8)

OVERVIEW:ELIZAJANE (5) is a smart performer for trainer-driver Tasmyn Potter, who has a great record with her small team. She finished fifth last start at Kilmore after being held up late, but she let down nicely once she had clear air. Her previous start was a nice win at Shepparton. With some luck from the barrier, she’s a massive winning chance. JOHN WAYNE (1) steps out for the 100th time here. He’s been a bit unlucky in his recent runs, but that should change here with his good barrier. JILLIBY ILLUSION (6) was an OK third behind the smart DEMBE last start at Shepparton. He is racing well but will need to overcome the tricky barrier. MOMENTUM SHIFT (4), KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3) and MAXY CAN DANCE (2) are also good options for the exotics if they get a good run. BACK: ELIZAJANE (5)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: ELIZAJANE (5), JOHN WAYNE (1), JILLIBY ILLUSION (6), MOMENTUM SHIFT (4)

OVERVIEW:CLASSIC FAIR (7) was second last start at Shepparton. He found the front at the 400m but was run down by 1.9 metres later by the smart Abbie. He has ability when he puts it all together, but his manners are a concern. MOONSHINE LOUIE (4) is a consistent performer who has rarely finished outside the top five recently. He will need some luck to win, but he is racing well. WHITERING (5) is a pacing-bred trotter who has had only two career starts. On debut, he won at Cranbourne when sprinting along the sprint lane. Last start, he looked to be running well in the breeze at Maryborough but galloped under pressure late. He clearly has ability, but he looks to wear spreaders, so it’s likely he hits his knee, which is a slight worry over the tight Echuca track. SYDTHESLOTH (3) is second-up here, and I am expecting an improved performance with added fitness following his first-up fourth at Shepparton, where he travelled well and let down nicely. BACK: CLASSIC FAIR (7)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: CLASSIC FAIR (7), MOONSHINE LOUIE (4), WHITERING (5), SYDTHESLOTH (3) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:MYSTIC MOTIVER (2) and EVA EXPRESS (1) have the best recent sectional times in this field. MYSTIC MOTIVER (2) has had three starts this preparation, finishing fifth last start after two consecutive seconds. She let down nicely last time but couldn’t make up enough ground in a 27.2 last quarter. It was an encouraging performance, and she looks well placed here. EVA EXPRESS (1) has had just three career starts, producing adequate performances so far. Barrier one is a positive, giving her the opportunity to make the most of the inside draw. TAMALIA (3) has good gate speed and, with only four career starts under her belt, has scope to improve with further fitness and experience. SPOT THE DEVIL (7) has shown improved form since joining the Mark Watson stable and looks ready to break through for his maiden victory. His barrier is the main challenge. SELECTIONS: MYSTIC MOTIVER (2), EVA EXPRESS (1), TAMALIA (3), SPOT THE DEVIL (7)

OVERVIEW:HARLEY LANE (9) is a smart mare trained by Jayne Davies who is first up since December 2025. She has shown plenty of ability, finishing just 12.8 metres from the winner in last year’s Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final for three-year-old fillies. She has had three trials this year and, from barrier nine, can follow through early into a handy position without being used up. LORIMERMAJOR (2) has been racing well and looks to be working towards a return to the winners’ circle. If he can map well from barrier two and avoid a tough run, he can be in the finish. MILEY KAY (6) has had just four career starts and looks a smart filly. She was dominant when finding the front and winning her maiden last start. This is a step up in class, and finding the front again could be difficult. SPUN SILVER (5) is a flashy, high-speed grey mare who underperformed last start. If she can bounce back to her best and find some luck, she is worth considering for the exotics. FRESH PRINCE (8) is also one to note, having his first start for new trainer Mick Carbone. BACK: HARLEY LANE (9)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: HARLEY LANE (9), LORIMERMAJOR (2), MILEY KAY (6), SPUN SILVER (5)

OVERVIEW:RAKAROMPA (9) is a talented but lightly raced mare returning to the track for the first time since June. She has had three solid trials leading into this assignment and, at her best, can run the fastest times in this field. Barrier nine also suits. SPEEDY HEALEY (4) rarely runs a bad race and, much like his namesake, can show plenty of speed when saved for one run. YELLA (1) has been consistent, finishing in the top five at every start since June. She led last start but was run down late by the swoopers. The inside draw suits, giving her the opportunity to race on the fence. CALYPSO MISTRESS (5) is first up but has had three trials in preparation for her return. Fitness remains the query, although she is a competitive and consistent type. SELECTIONS: RAKAROMPA (9), SPEEDY HEALEY (4), YELLA (1), CALYPSO MISTRESS (5)

OVERVIEW:LIBERTY STAR DUST (2) looks a good each-way play in this event. She should have enough gate speed to find the fence early and, despite doing it tough in a decent race last start, she has the best sectional times in this field. She has been out of the winners’ circle for a while, but her sectionals suggest she has the ability to make her presence felt. BILLYS TIGER KHAN (8) is a very talented horse and will likely be the favourite in this event. He improved a nice winner last start after a long time on the sidelines. He will improve again from that run. HELLO POSSUMS (1) can have a line drawn through her last start, as she had no clear running late but looked to be travelling well. She is racing nicely and will get a good trip here on the fence. POSTERIZED (4) gives Talia Taugge her first start as a driver here, so best of luck to Talia! Posterized is a nice horse for Kate and Andy Gath who ran a tough second last start at Melton, narrowly beaten late after racing in the breeze. BACK: LIBERTY STAR DUST (2) – 1 unit (win)/ 2 units (place) SELECTIONS: LIBERTY STAR DUST (2), BILLYS TIGER KHAN (8), HELLO POSSUMS (1), POSTERIZED (4)

OVERVIEW:ROYAL LADY (10) is a New Zealand-bred trotter who has had three career starts in Australia for Brent Lilley. She got it wrong with her manners on debut, but showed what she can do two starts ago when doing everything right in a tougher field and battling on well. She made another costly mistake last start, but her effort was eye-catching. After galloping early and losing considerable ground, she recovered and flashed home to be beaten by just half a neck. The ability is there, but she needs to put it all together and trot throughout. BIRMINGHAM GIRL (5) has had just one career start, finishing third at Cranbourne. She let down nicely once clear late and should improve with that experience under her belt. PASTOR JAY JAY (8) is a first starter for trainer John Justice. He looked good winning a trial last start, sprinting home along the sprint lane. We will learn more about him after this run. BELIEVE IN SUNNY (6) returned with a pleasing third last start after racing in the breeze and fighting on well late. He should improve here with added fitness. BACK: ROYAL LADY (10) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: ROYAL LADY (10), BIRMINGHAM GIRL (5), PASTOR JAY JAY (8), BELIEVE IN SUNNY (6)

OVERVIEW:KYVALLEY MISTY (4) has been racing well and deserves some luck. Two starts ago at Maryborough, she had a tough run in the breeze in rain-affected conditions but still battled on well for second. Last start, she sustained a three-wide trip and was beaten by just 4.3 metres. She is going well and will be hoping for a more favourable race map here. KIMBERLEYS TREE (9) has the best sectional times in this field and possesses plenty of ability when she puts it all together. However, bad luck and occasional mistakes with her manners have affected her recent results, leaving her numerical form looking less impressive. Barrier nine suits, and if she can trot throughout, she will be a major threat. JESSICAS STORY (6) had a tough run at Maryborough last start but remained strong and determined late to finish third. She is a nice horse, although the barrier makes things tricky. CHRISTMAS BABE (2) has good gate speed and should map well from this draw. The race distance also suits her. SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY MISTY (4), KIMBERLEYS TREE (9), JESSICAS STORY (6), CHRISTMAS BABE (2)

OVERVIEW:CHASING THE WIND (3) is racing better than his numerical form suggests. He endured a very tough run in the breeze last start and, despite finishing last, it was far from a disappointing performance. If he can map well here, he has an opportunity to turn his form around. FAKE CULLECTION (8) is an interesting mare who can be a little inconsistent and occasionally gets it wrong with her manners. She tired last start, but when she puts it all together, she is capable of a good performance. At her best, she is a winning chance. DELTA STARZ (5) drops in class for this event but will need some luck from the barrier. UNETHICAL (2) comes out of barrier one following the scratching of the horse inside her. She is lightly raced, having had just five starts this year, and produced one of the best runs of her career last start. From barrier one, she was shuffled back on the fence but hit the line well to finish fifth. She gets another opportunity here, with the prospect of a similar race map helping her build on that effort with confidence. ROCKNROLL RAMBO (11) and TASTE IT (10) also deserve respect. SELECTIONS: CHASING THE WIND (3), FAKE CULLECTION (8), DELTA STARZ (5), UNETHICAL (2)

OVERVIEW:WAIKARE ADRIENNA (2) is a nice trotter who made an impressive return to the winners’ circle last start. Second up, she raced in the breeze before forging clear late to score convincingly. That effort came from barrier seven, and she should be better placed here from barrier two. ABBIE (4) had a tough run last start and tired late, but her previous effort was encouraging. She flashed home impressively from midfield to win and will be looking to build on that performance. FRANKS A LOT (6) is a promising trotter who has made a strong impression in his first two career starts. He finished a strong second on debut after racing in the breeze, then sustained a three-wide trip last start to win impressively. He faces a tricky barrier here, and each start will bring tougher challenges. WALLIS (9) finds a suitable barrier to follow through early and be saved for a late sprint. SELECTIONS: WAIKARE ADRIENNA (2), ABBIE (4), FRANKS A LOT (6), WALLIS (9)

OVERVIEW:I SEA RED (7) is a talented gelding returning for his first start since February. Now three, he showed plenty of promise as a young horse while racing against some talented horses in his age group. Barrier seven makes his return tricky, but he looks the standout performer in this field. BUNGY (8) has produced recent performances that look close to his best and appears ready to return to the winners’ circle. The barrier is awkward, however. BEAU BECA (2) looks likely to map better than his main rivals, with the opportunity to find the fence and make the most of a favourable trip. He is racing well enough to capitalise if things fall into place. THESTING (6) is an interesting runner who remains lightly raced. He galloped early in each of his first two starts this campaign. Last start, the horse in front of him galloped, forcing him to check, so he was not at fault. He showed promise earlier in his career and could turn his form around here. I am also expecting an improved performance from THE PRIVATE DEAL (10). BACK: I SEA RED (7)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: I SEA RED (7), BUNGY (8), BEAU BECA (2), THESTING (6)

OVERVIEW:WOODLEA DIEGO (3) comes out of barrier two following the scratching of the horse drawn in barrier one. He let down nicely at Ballarat last start but had little clear running late. If he can map well here, he finds a suitable race. SENNA STORM (2) gets the ideal opportunity for a fence run from barrier one following the scratching of the horse inside him. He finished seventh when first up last start and was clearly beaten, unable to make up ground late. However, he is capable of capitalising on the right run at his best, and he should get his chance from the inside gate here. KNOW THE SCORE (8) gets one more chance from me. He got it wrong with his manners two starts ago and tired quite uncharacteristically last start, although his previous runs were good. At his best, he is a nice horse in a field like this, but there are some questions about where he is at. ONECROWDEDHOUR (9) was first up last start, got well back and let down well late. He should improve from that run. SELECTIONS: WOODLEA DIEGO (3), SENNA STORM (2), KNOW THE SCORE (8), ONECROWDEDHOUR (9) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:CHALKNCHEDDAR (5) settled three back on the markers and tried hard for third behind Talknplay at Swan Hill last outing. He appears to be very well placed against this field and is versatile enough to overcome the wide draw. STONEBRIDGE STAR (2) finished off fairly well for third behind Keayang Crippa at Mildura on October 20. This race is a little easier and he is worth thought again. DIAMOND KRUSHER (6) is a fast beginner and is a good chance of finding the lead despite being drawn on the outside of the front line. He led throughout at a Mildura victory on September 04 so he cannot be left out of calculations. BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (7) missed out at Swan Hill last week but he ran a very good race for second behind Talknplay (won again since) three starts ago so he is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: CHALKNCHEDDAR (5), STONEBRIDGE STAR (2), DIAMOND KRUSHER (6), BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (7)

OVERVIEW:LITLMAX (3) was driven with plenty of confidence on debut where she was headed off from the pole position and moved up without cover from the 1600m. She has ability and strikes a suitable field so she can go one better here. LATHER WITH FIRE (5) broke stride and lost her chance at her latest distant fourth but she has won a trial at Shepparton since and is a possible improver. CRUEL MISTRESS (6) finished off reasonably well from midfield when third behind Phils Boy in a race of similar standard last outing. She is widely drawn but is not without a chance. BRIEISBETTER (7) is an experienced maiden having had 65 attempts but she has been placed in two of her past three starts and she should enjoy an economical run from her trailing draw. BACK: LITLMAX (3) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: LITLMAX (3), LATHER WITH FIRE (5), CRUEL MISTRESS (6), BRIEISBETTER (7)

OVERVIEW: THE LADYBIRD (2) did very well after being in the uncharacteristic role of parking without cover at her latest Kilmore third. She recorded a mile rate of 1.57.7 when she scored at Horsham prior and she should prove hard to beat again. HESASTAR (3) is a fast beginner and should give a forward showing from his good draw. He worked forward to find the lead and scored comfortably at Mildura on September 18. KEAYANG CRIPPA (5) gained a nice trail and finished off best to snare victory over HESASTAR (3) last outing. He is usually competitive against this class and is worth thought again. ROJENBYE (8) picked up some ground from midfield when fourth at Charlton last outing and is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: THE LADYBIRD (2), HESASTAR (3), KEAYANG CRIPPA (5), ROJENBYE (8)

OVERVIEW: BRANSON (2) is a capable South Australian trained pacer, which led throughout to win in a mile rate of 1.57.3 at Gawler two starts ago. He is a good chance of finding the lead again and will take catching over the sprint distance. SUNSHINE WARRIOR (1) led throughout at a Mildura victory three starts ago and she didn’t have the best of luck from a wide alley at her latest fifth. She should receive the perfect trip from the pole position and is worth an investment. ASHANTE WARRIOR (7) is making his Mildura debut but his form in the South-East has been strong enough to be competitive against this class. He led throughout in a mile rate of 1.57.8 three starts ago. MASON DIXON LINE (3) hasn’t been able to draw on the front line for a long time so he gets his chance to improve under these conditions. SELECTIONS: BRANSON (2), SUNSHINE WARRIOR (1), ASHANTE WARRIOR (7), MASON DIXON LINE (3)

OVERVIEW:CELESTIAL STARLET (6) is a 2yo filly on debut but she has shaped up nicely at the trials with a win and a third at Maryborough to her credit. She obviously has ability and is likely to be strongly fancied. MISTER HENDRIX (5) has been unplaced in all of this three starts to date but his trial form is far stronger than his race form. He strikes a suitable assignment at his first run since March and he is worth respect. MISS CULLEN (7) trailed the leader and dropped out at the end when last of seven at Swan Hill last outing. She met a much stronger field last time out and was runner up at her previous two attempts so she must be considered as a place hope again. THE MIGHTY CAESAR (3) is a first starter for trainer Boris Devcic, which has had numerous trial attempts and is worth thought in multiple combinations. SELECTIONS: CELESTIAL STARLET (6), MISTER HENDRIX (5),MISS CULLEN (7), THE MIGHTY CAESAR (3)

OVERVIEW:RUFF NUT (6) progressed forward to race without cover and fought on strongly when a brave second behind Chase The Stars at Globe Derby last outing. He is a tough campaigner and looms as one of the leading chances. DALLAS MIKI (8) is a bold front running pacer, which is unsuited being drawn on the second row but is sure to make his presence felt. He was held up for a run at a vital stage and locked wheels momentarily turning for home when an unlucky fourth in the Swan Hill Cup last week. THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) is racing in career best form but this is his toughest test to date. He sustained a long run when he got up to defeat Keayang Shadowbox at Mildura last outing. ROYAL SAXON (3) settled in the second half of the field and tried to sustain a long run from the 800m when a game third at Mildura last outing. He should go well again from his good draw. SELECTIONS: RUFF NUT (6), DALLAS MIKI (8), THE GOLDEN HOOK (7), ROYAL SAXON (3)

OVERVIEW: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (5) settled in the second half of the field and finished off strongly for a game third in the Swan Hill Cup last week. He led throughout to win comfortably when resuming at Mildura on September 30 and is clearly the horse to beat again. HOT DEAL (7) commenced from the inside of the second line, was held up behind tiring runners and finished off fairly well for fifth at Globe Derby last outing. He boasts a very strong record at Mildura and will run his usual honest race if he has normal luck in running from the awkward draw. PRIORITISE (8) settled in the second half of the field, came out three horses wide over the latter stages and produced a strong finish to win at Mildura last outing. This race is of similar standard and he looms as one of the leading chances again. MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (1) is a strong pacer, which will take tossing if he can hold a forward position at the start. He was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off solidly for a close up third at Swan Hill last outing. BACK: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (5), HOT DEAL (7), PRIORITISE (8), MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (1)

OVERVIEW: ARMOURY (6) is a former New South Wales pacer, which joins trainer Alex Ashwood. She was shuffled back in the field mid-race and failed to run on at Penrith last outing but was a winner on that track three starts ago and strikes a suitable assignment at her Mildura debut. EAGLEYE (1) has been placed in four of her past five starts and is perfectly drawn to run a good race again. She commenced from the inside of the second line, was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off well for second at Swan Hill last outing. LORD MYRMECIA (8) failed to run on as expected at Kapunda last outing but he finished fast for an eye-catching second at Globe Derby prior and has performed well at Mildura previously so he cannot be left out of calculations. CELESTIAL NEBULAE (10) has the ability to figure in the finish but he wanted to hang in badly on the bends at Globe Derby last outing so being drawn on the second line will be a disadvantage. SELECTIONS: ARMOURY (6), EAGLEYE (1), LORD MYRMECIA (8), CELESTIAL NEBULAE (10)

OVERVIEW: BETTORBUST (3) finished second behind the smart pacer Delizioso at Shepparton last outing and was a runaway winner at Mildura prior. He is the class runner of the field and will prove extremely hard to beat. CAULONIA TERROR (4) settled three back on the markers, got caught up behind tiring horses and lost approximately five lengths with 700m remaining so he did well to recover and finish in third behind Lower Manhattan last outing. He was unlucky in that performance and is worth a ticket each way. FLAME BLASTER (2) performs best when he is able to trail the leader so he is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern. He was runner up from behind the leader last outing and is a strong place chance again. OZZIE DAYBREAK (9) has performed extremely well in two starts back from a spell and rates as a value hope. BACK: BETTORBUST (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETTORBUST (3), CAULONIA TERROR (4), FLAME BLASTER (2), OZZIE DAYBREAK (9)

OVERVIEW: BANDIT EYES (9) endured a tough run and dropped out at Metropolitan level last outing. He led throughout to score in a sizzling mile rate of 1.53.2 at Melton back in August and is the class runner of this field. MIDNIGHT PIRATE (2) was caught wide early, restrained to being five back on the markers mid-race and worked home well for fourth at Swan Hill last outing. He is a fast beginner and is racing in good form so a bold showing is expected. HAPPY AS CAN BE (5) competed in the South Australian Cup series, where seventh in the Final so he is likely to find this race to be easier. He had his chance when second at Globe Derby last week but warrants consideration. SHIRLEY NOT (6) is racing in career best form and is worth thought along with the handy sprinter GOOD BOOTS BINDI (7). BACK: BANDIT EYES (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BANDIT EYES (9), MIDNIGHT PIRATE (2), HAPPY AS CAN BE (5), GOOD BOOTS BINDI (7)

OVERVIEW: First heat of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup here where plenty can win, but I’ll side with ANAKIN (2) for Team Shinn. He has been caught parked his last two at Kilmore, but boxed on bravely to not be beaten far. If he can find the fence, he should be fighting out the finish as his best is pretty good in this grade. TED BEAR (3) was a good winner at Melton last time out and all his recent form is sound, GENERAL ROCKER (6) ran well first-up for trainer Glenn Beale to only be beaten 10.8m in a fast race at Kilmore on October 22 and might be one to consider at likely good odds, while COOL STORY (10) dug deep to win as favourite from the chair at Ballarat back on October 7 and is certainly a winning chance with the right trip and tempo from wide on the back line. SELECTIONS: ANAKIN (2), TED BEAR (3), GENERAL ROCKER (6), COOL STORY (10)

OVERVIEW: RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (4) has been very close to breaking his maiden on a number of occasions and is presented with another great chance here. He has done things wrong in recent starts but has still managed close-up minor placings his last four outings and certainly looks capable of taking a race like this on his best behaviour. COGNAC COWBOY (1) produced a big finale from back in the field to just miss last start at Kilmore and draws for a lovely trip here, DIAMOND CHIPP (3) finished alongside RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (4) at Geelong two back and wasn’t too bad when fourth last start at Kilmore, while HILLCROFT HUSTLER (7) was good on debut when second to a handy one in Winchester Boy at Cranbourne and is among the winning chances alongside BAD GRANDMA (6) and perhaps BANIA (9), who trialled well and started odds-on on debut at Geelong but dropped out sharply after a tough trip last time at Melton. SELECTIONS: RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (4), COGNAC COWBOY (1), DIAMOND CHIPP (3), HILLCROFT HUSTLER (7)

OVERVIEW: OUR TINKA BELLE (6) is a five-year-old who only made her debut back in July, but has shown loads of ability despite plenty of issues with her manners. Two back at Geelong, she looked home in the straight at massive odds before galloping in the shadows of the post. And last time at Kilmore, she was held up in the last lap but unleashed a big finale to round up her rivals and win softly on the line under minimal driving from Jack Laugher. She’s taking on much more experienced rivals in this Bacchus Marsh Trotters Cup heat, but I think there’s some good ability there. DOSSIER (9) drops back slightly in grade and brings in some strong formlines, stablemate JOE LOU (7) has loads of talent but has broken his last two and is a risky trotter, while JAKARTA (10) has been competitive of late and is the highest rated trotter in the field at 55 so must be respected. BACK: OUR TINKA BELLE (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: OUR TINKA BELLE (6), DOSSIER (9), JOE LOU (7), JAKARTA (10)

OVERVIEW: WEONA OUR RIGHTS (8) has been in good form for Adam Shaw in recent weeks with a string of close-up efforts at Cranbourne and Melton. Last time, he was only beaten 5.7m into second by the handy Kosimo and had chased home in-form rivals such as Quick Crunch, Cyclone Jenni and Blazin By before that. Just needs the right trip to be going close, and he might get it if ANIMADO (1) kicks up and holds the top. ANIMADO (1) settled at the rear of the field from a wide barrier and charged late to be beaten just a head at Shepparton last time out. It was a good effort, and from the pole draw he’s a chance at start 150. ROSBERG (2) seems to often end up racing in the chair, but did win from that position in good style at Melton back in late September, while MIDNIGHT MOJO (5) is racing consistently well of late and is another of the key winning chances alongside FLIGHT LOUTENANT (7). BACK: WEONA OUR RIGHTS (8) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: WEONA OUR RIGHTS (8), ANIMADO (1), ROSBERG (2), MIDNIGHT MOJO (5)

OVERVIEW: Second heat of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup and it’s another wide-open event where most of the runners have claims. QUICK CRUNCH (8) brings in the winning form following back-to-back triumphs at Cranbourne and Ballarat, and looks a good chance of making it three on end despite the inside back row draw. She has run solid last halves in both those victories from the fence and should be fighting out the finish. SPORTS NARRATOR (9) was probably only fair first-up from a break at Ballarat on October 29 when fifth to Master Louey but ran some good races late last campaign and looks capable in this grade, FOREGONE CONCLUSION (2) just missed at Kilmore last time when coming from back in the field and is a very honest customer who has won 26 career races, while CORNISHTOWN KID (5) has been going okay of late in perhaps slightly stronger company and can figure with the right trip. SELECTIONS: QUICK CRUNCH (8), SPORTS NARRATOR (9), FOREGONE CONCLUSION (2), CORNISHTOWN KID (5)

OVERVIEW: WHIRLY MAURZ (3) has a runner-up placing and dominant victory to her name since joining the Andy Gath stable, and will likely go around as a warm favourite in this clash. Last week at Ballarat, she settled in the one-one and bolted away from her rivals – including IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1) and THE MOUNTAIN (5) – to break her maiden by a huge margin at start 34. She can win again in this company. RIDDLEMETHIS (7) looks the key danger to her chances after a good three-start campaign so far. He managed two placings at Kilmore and a tough Ballarat win through October and should run well despite the wide gate. FREAK OUT (4) and IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1) are next best, but a result outside the top two fancies would surprise. SELECTIONS: WHIRLY MAURZ (3), RIDDLEMETHIS (7), FREAK OUT (4), IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1)

OVERVIEW: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (2) has started her latest campaign with back-to-back victories at Geelong and Melton, and this shapes as another very winnable assignment. She was a tad lucky to score at Geelong when the leader galloped in the shadows of the post, but her latest effort when parked at Melton was outstanding. She charged clear there and won softly by 18.2m in a dominant performance. Happy her way. KISS AT MIDNIGHT (4) probably has the speed to lead this race, but her manners have been awful in recent times with gallops in the past four outings. Her best is good enough, but she’s very hard to trust at the moment. MAJESTIC CHARMA (6) led and faded late in what was just a fair effort last time at Maryborough but has won seven career races and two this campaign, while AI SEDHAI (3) and AHUNDREDPLUS (5) might be best of the rest, but victory would probably surprise. BACK: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (2) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (2), KISS AT MIDNIGHT (4), MAJESTIC CHARMA (6), AI SEDHAI (3)

OVERVIEW: Tough way to end the night at Melton, but REASON TO LAUGH (7) gets the nod despite the wide front row draw. Last start at Ballarat, he was trapped three wide for the last lap but actually did a great job to soldier on and only be beaten 7.5m in a slick enough last half for this grade of 57.7sec. The run before that was a well-beaten second to handy rival Talknplay, and there are good wins earlier in the month at Cranbourne and Kilmore through his recent form. ARE WEASLEY (5) is another of the leading contenders after finding the winner’s stall at his last outing at Kilmore when closing off nicely from the one-one for Connor Clarke, there’s a big watch on MAMMALS BLAZE (6) who is now in the care of trainer Joe Pace and won his first trial for the stable at Bacchus Marsh in preparation for this, while GOZO MAJOR (4) and OUR TRUE COLOURS (3) are other hopes in an even contest to close the meeting. BACK: REASON TO LAUGH (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: REASON TO LAUGH (7), ARE WEASLEY (5), MAMMALS BLAZE (6), GOZO MAJOR (4) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R3 #6 OUR TINKA BELLE – 2 units (win) R4 #8 WEONA OUR RIGHTS – 1.5 units (each-way) R7 #2 BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE – 3 units (win) R8 #7 REASON TO LAUGH – 2 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 2,3,5,6,7,8,10/1,3,4,6,7/6,7,9/1,2,5,8 QUADDIE 2,5,8,9/3,7/2,4,6/4,5,6,7 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

CHARLIE CHUCKLES (1) led two starts ago at Marburg and was run down late by Taylors Four who had the perfect run on his back. He draws favourably in this race and can look to drive through early and hold the lead at a track and trip he seems to be suited at. ASHLEE NITRO (7) bounced back two starts ago to score another Redcliffe victory before having much less luck last time out in a race taken out by The Tiger Army. She should get a good run through early and won’t be far away. ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (4) secured a good run behind the speed last time out and was running on fairly late into fourth. She appears to find a suitable race but does draw a touch awkwardly. KUZMA (6) secured a good run behind the speed two starts ago and was running on well late into second behind Sweet Lad Jujon. He should get a good run off the speed in this race and can be running on late again. SELECTIONS: CHARLIE CHUCKLES (1), ASHLEE NITRO (7), ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (4), KUZMA (6) SUGGESTED BET: CHARLIE CHUCKLES (1) to win.

CALL KELLY (9) has really bounced back into some form in recent outings and was able to score an impressive win her latest outing when sweeping over the top late to score beating Wait What. She looks set to get a good run off the speed again in this race and should be running on late again. THE TORQUE EFFECT (4) looks likely to be shuffled back a touch early in this race from a slightly awkward draw. She put in another excellent run last time out when being caught wide on the way home in a race the leader ran a quick last half for the grade and was still able to run a good third behind Im Busted. REAL MIKI (2) has a reasonable front row draw and may look to press forward and find a prominent position. He was running on nicely into third last time out behind Holme Boy and Littlemickey. DIGBY DEVIL (7) draws awkwardly inside the back row in this race. He secured a good run three starts ago and finished best there to score beating Need Not To Worry. SELECTIONS: CALL KELLY (9),THE TORQUE EFFECT (4), REAL MIKI (2), DIGBY DEVIL (7) SUGGESTED BET: THE TORQUE EFFECT (4) to win.

SWEET NELLIE JOY (1) led in a much stronger race last time out and was beaten a long way there behind Race For Riches. She steps back to the 1780 at Redcliffe where she has run well previously and should be hard to run down. OUR ULTIMATE JESSY (5) was a metro winner last time out when leading all the way at Albion Park. She draws less favourably this time but should find this no tougher and should be hard to beat again in this race. REAL TIN TIN (7) got back in the run last time out and was running on late not beaten far behind Merry Jewel. He looks likely to get a good run through early in this race and should be running on late. ROCK NIEN (6) draws awkwardly outside the front row in this race but does look one of the class runners in this field. He led all the way three starts ago and has since raced with less luck. SELECTIONS: SWEET NELLIE JOY (1), OUR ULTIMATE JESSY (5), REAL TIN TIN (7), ROCK NIEN (6) SUGGESTED BET: SWEET NELLIE JOY (1) to win.

ERASMUS (1) has reasonable gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in the early stages of this race from a good draw. He couldn’t quite get across to the pegs last time out before being left without cover in a race taken out by The Real Rocketman. This looks easier and he can lead this time. SNIP OF BEAUTY (3) didn’t look to have a lot of luck last time out when badly held up at a crucial stage in a race taken out by Miss Hattie. She should settle close and with more luck can play a part in the finish. DOOO DONT THINK (4) was shuffled a long way back last time out at this track before hitting the line nicely late in a race taken out by October Racketeer. He should settle close enough from a front row draw and can be running on late. HIGHVIEW SADLER (8) worked forward early last time out before being shuffled back and was still able to run on late into fourth. He should settle close in this race from a soft trailing draw and can look to be running on late again. SELECTIONS: ERASMUS (1), SNIP OF BEAUTY (3), DOOO DONT THINK (4), HIGHVIEW SADLER (8) SUGGESTED BET: HIGHVIEW SADLER (8) each way.

HOLME BOY (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in the early stages of this race. He ran well two starts ago when being run down late by Ashlee Nitro before proving too good last time out when running over the top to beat Littlemickey. MY SCIMITAR (7) made a break at Albion Park early on Monday and will find himself ODM as a result in this race. He should still get a good run close to the speed and can be running on late again. DIEGO DELGADO (4) was forced to race without cover last time out and battled on for a good third there behind October Racketeer and Last Call. He should settle close enough and can run well again. SHEEZ GOT TORQUE (2) was able to lead and win two starts ago after controlling things out in front. It doesn’t appear she will be able to lead again but she should still settle close enough to figure in the finish. SELECTIONS: HOLME BOY (1), MY SCIMITAR (7), DIEGO DELGADO (4), SHEEZ GOT TORQUE (2) SUGGESTED BET: HOLME BOY (1) to win.

GOLDCLASS (9) sat behind the leader on debut and battled on well there behind Fan The Flame. She should get a good run off the speed in this race and should be running on well late. TASK AT HAND (3) wasn’t suited last time out when coming off the pegs early in a race which was dominated by runners on the pegs close to the speed. She looks likely to be able to press forward early in this race and if she could lead she can give them something to catch. ILLBERIDINGSHOTGUN (5) got back from a wide draw last time out and was running on late into fourth. He may be shuffled back again in this race and can be running on late. STRAWBERRIESNCREAM (2) doesn’t appear to have much gate speed which could see her shuffled back a touch. She secured a good run last time out and battled on fairly fifth. SELECTIONS: GOLDCLASS (9), TASK AT HAND (3), ILLBERIDINGSHOTGUN (5), STRAWBERRIESNCREAM (2) SUGGESTED BET: GOLDCLASS (9) to win.

THE TIGER ARMY (1) has moderate gate speed and may be able to drive through and lead early in this race. He was able to score a big win last time out over the 2040 rating fast time there. He should be hard to beat. STORMTIDE (3) was able to secure a good run two starts ago and sprinted best at this track to score a nice win. He should secure a nice run off the speed again in this race and can be running on late. WELEASE WODDEWICK (6) had an issue last start and was stood down to trial there and has since trialled fairly running third. He draws poorly and will need a few things to go his way. PRETTY LITTLE LIAR (4) ran a good race last time out when finishing third behind Major Crunch and Gem Punter Pete. She has good gate speed and may look for a prominent position early in this race. SELECTIONS: THE TIGER ARMY (1), STORMTIDE (3), WELEASE WODDEWICK (6), PRETTY LITTLE LIAR (4) SUGGESTED BET: THE TIGER ARMY (1) to win.

AIR FORCE ONE (1) appeared to run the gate reasonably initially last time out before restraining to the rear of the field and was running on well into fourth behind Louark and FREE REIGN (3). He should run well from an ideal draw. FREE REIGN (3) was forced to race without cover last time out and ran well there finishing second to Louark. He looks likely to be left doing the work again in this race and should run well again. WAIT WHAT (4) secured a good run behind the speed last time out and was running on late into second behind Call Kelly. He comes into this race third up and should run well again. ZEUSTORM (7) appears likely to get a favourable run through early in this race behind a horse which is likely to be keen to hold a forward position. He should appreciate what appears to be a drop in grade and can run well. SELECTIONS: AIR FORCE ONE (1), FREE REIGN (3), WAIT WHAT (4), ZEUSTORM (7) SUGGESTED BET: AIR FORCE ONE (1) to win.
